drone: quadrotor of unstated make (AVQ, Wang/Sanchez-Matilla/Cavallaro IROS 2019), on a camera tripod; 8-mic ring (~0.18 m) on posts 15 cm above the arms, GoPro at the array centre
frame: mic_pos.mat frame: origin = array centre, x = 0 deg and y = 90 deg axes of array_configuration.docx (angle_a counter-clockwise from +x seen from above), z up; metres. The drone's forward axis (top-view 0 deg = camera optical axis) lies at angle_a = a2 (S1 -28.23 deg, S2 -29.08 deg).

mic_pos.basis: publisher mic_pos.mat values (0.1 mm); ring mount tolerance

rotor_pos.basis: drone-frame hub layout: least-squares residual of the five publisher distances <= 0.4 cm, photo-measured layout differs by <= 1.2 cm; forward axis +-1 deg (photo registration vs a2) = +-0.5 cm at 0.3 m; array-centre projection onto the arm plane (photo parallax) +-2 cm; prop plane 14-19 cm below the mic-frame origin depending on which platform.jpg scale is trusted

sources: .cache/avq_docs/raw/S1__misc__mic_pos (mic_pos.mat, 3 x 8, metres; identical in S1 and S2)

.cache/avq_docs/platform.jpg (side view: ring 20 cm wide, ~15 cm above the arms; top view: 0 deg forward, 90 deg right; hub distances front pair 45 cm, rear pair 41 cm, left side 26 cm, centre->front-right 24 cm, centre->rear-left 28 cm; 2D-coordinates panel: O_M = O_C, theta from the forward z-axis towards +x/right)
avq_S1.notes: Derivation. (1) Drone-frame hub layout (X right, Y forward, origin = array centre projected on the arm plane): left/right symmetry about the 0-deg axis (photo: hubs at -185/+185 px and -175/+175 px from the axis) and the pair distances give X = +-0.225 (front) / +-0.205 (rear); Y from least squares of |centre-FR| = 0.24, |centre-RL| = 0.28, |FL-RL| = 0.26: Y_front = +0.072, Y_rear = -0.188 (residuals <= 0.4 cm; photo at 8.45 +- 0.26 px/cm gives +0.068 / -0.200). The array centre sits ~6.6 cm ahead of the rotor centroid. (2) Orientation: forward (top-view 0 deg) is at angle_a = a2 of av_calibration.mat (-28.23 deg for S1), right = a2 - 90 deg (angle_a counter-clockwise from +x seen from above, z up). Independent check: a 2-D similarity fit of mic_pos (x, y) to the 7 visible mic blobs of the platform.jpg top view (exhaustive cyclic correspondences, both handednesses) gives rms 3.05 px at 1026.2 px/m (~3 mm), not mirrored (best mirrored fit 9.19 px), blob->mic {'G': 3, 'E': 5, 'D': 7, 'B': 2, 'A': 6, 'C': 1, 'F': 8}, and puts image-up (forward) at angle_a = -28.52 deg - within 0.3/0.6 deg of a2 (S1/S2). This also confirms that the mic_pos frame is right-handed with z up as seen in the photo. (3) Height: rotor_pos z = -0.15 m (publisher's 15 cm ring-to-arm label; mic-frame origin is at the upper mic level, mics span z -0.032..+0.004). Rotor positions are hub centres; labels front/rear = towards/away from the camera axis.

open_questions: Channel map (channel i = mic i+1) is assumed by file order.
Assumed: the publisher's top-view 0 deg axis is both the camera optical axis and the drone's forward symmetry axis (supported: the photo registration lands within 0.6 deg of a2).
The 15 cm ring-to-arm height and the photo scales disagree (side-view vertical vs horizontal scale differ by ~35 %); the prop plane is 0.14-0.19 m below the mic-frame origin.

The array-centre projection onto the arm plane is taken at the crossing of the publisher's dashed axes (where its 24/28 cm arrows start); the fitted ring centre in the photo is 25.5 px forward of it (~3 cm at the arm-plane scale), attributed to parallax of the 15 cm higher ring.
Whether the array or drone was remounted between S1 and S2 is not stated (a2 differs by 0.85 deg).
